card.name: Mixed spots in warnings and drug names
card.fires_on: Mostly the word "to" after "their ability" in driving and machinery cautions. It also fires inside some drug names, such as Etonogestrel, naloxone and ANZUPGO, and on odd words like "watched" in a story.

modes.label: Ability to in caution text
modes.description: The word "to" after "affect their ability" in warnings about driving or hazardous activities.
modes.example: does not adversely affect their ability<< to>> engage in such activities.

modes.label: Inside drug names
modes.description: A middle piece of a drug or brand name, such as naloxone or etonogestrel.
modes.example: The<< nal>>oxone challenge test should not be performed

modes.label: Stray word in narrative
modes.description: A verb in casual prose after a conditional, as in "I would have watched my step".
modes.example: Forewarned, I would have<< watched>> my step.

card.writes: The suppressed tokens are about routine checks and risk, and the promoted ones are about rescue. The output effect is weak and unclear.
card.plain: It mostly marks the word "to" in "ability to drive or operate machinery" warnings, plus some drug-name pieces.
